tasks.completion_note: Had to minimize an EOF fixture before the Rust harness would reproduce it.

pdf.title: Bounded event decoding · a porting practical

sections.heading: What has already been ported
sections.body: The service writes a compact length-prefixed ring of status events. A production backup tool uses the old C reader; the prototype uses a Rust iterator. The header is four bytes, little-endian. A zero payload length is a valid tombstone and consumes exactly the header. A payload may wrap at the physical end of the backing buffer. Neither language may read after the published tail, even if the allocation contains leftover bytes. The starter allocates a buffer and a separate logical cursor; tests exercise the same public Reader::next() method.

rows: Kind; unsupported values must produce InvalidKind
Flags. Retain unknown bits for the caller.

sections.heading: Reproduce before writing the fix
sections.body: Build the C reader with the supplied seed pack and retain one failing event transcript. Keep the seed and the ring capacity in the regression test name. Translate the failure to Rust. Treat cursor movement as an observable result: comparing the payload alone misses a second-call failure. Use a seed where the header is split and a distinct seed where only the payload wraps.

sections.heading: Deliverables and adversarial cases
sections.body: Implement wrap-safe parsing and a CLI exposing the first diverging cursor/value pair. Malformed lengths cannot advance the cursor. Add a paired regression covering a tombstone at the final four bytes and a positive payload ending at byte zero. Tests must verify the state before and after each read. Explain why the successful return path advances by the encoded length even when it represents an empty event. Also submit one minimized reproducer for a bug you encountered during the port.

sections.heading: Reporting-only exercise
sections.body: The course branch includes three archived transcripts for a separate write-up. Reuse the saved stdout and seed manifest. Extract the first bad cursor, summarize which decoder moved too early, and show the version of the corrected reader used for comparison. A passing output without the two cursor positions is incomplete. For the marked reporting exercise, students do not change source code or regenerate the logs.
sections.code:
cargo test --test replay -- wraps_header_then_tombstone
python scripts/compare_saved.py artifacts/baseline --key cursor_before

holdouts.title: Implement first divergence for C and Rust traces

holdouts.details: Only part I. My environment already builds both decoders.

pdf.title: Replay lab · Find the first divergent operation

sections.heading: Repository tour and deliverable
sections.body:
Your group maintains two decoders for a small write-ahead log. One decoder is C11 and the replacement is safe Rust. Their final checksums agree on the tiny smoke fixture even when they disagree about which logical entry was applied. Implement a bounded comparison tool the repair agent can call. The agent needs actionable context at the first mismatch without embedding a whole execution log in its prompt.

Start with replay/c_driver.c, crates/replay/src/reader.rs and tools/trace_diff.py. Both decoders already write UTF-8 JSON lines to separate files. You may change the Python tool and its registration only. Preserve the CLI and the existing public Rust signature. The tool receives two file paths and a nonnegative history limit, normally two. The grading fixtures include files longer than memory. Stream from each file once.

sections.heading: Input contract
sections.body: A line has integer seq, operation kind, an address or null, and an eight-character hexadecimal value. The sequence counts logical operations within a trace. Ignorable heartbeat records have kind tick and do not participate in equality or predecessor context. Normalize hexadecimal letters to lower case. A missing address is different from address zero. Preserve the original line number for diagnostic output. Empty lines may be skipped; a malformed nonblank line must return a parse error with side and line.

sections.heading: Part I · Implement and register the tool
sections.body:
Report match or first_difference, then give the most recent k matching logical operations, their source line numbers, and the next logical operation on each side. Return at most k predecessors in total. A missing side at end of file is a literal null. When one iterator ends early the command must check whether the other side has any remaining non-heartbeat records. Do not claim equality because a zip iterator stopped.

The stdout contract permits exactly one JSON object. Use exit status 0 for match or first_difference, 2 for malformed input and 3 for inaccessible files. Diagnostic text belongs on stderr. Wire the tool into the repair loop with a function description and argument schema. Record one real call and show how a repair would identify the source line. A partial parser without registration cannot earn integration credit.

sections.heading: Acceptance cases
sections.body: Distribute the named regression cases across unit and CLI tests. Check structure and line numbers by parsing the JSON. Include one example where no code change is required because the normalized operations match.

rows: Different heartbeat placement and hex case
Rust trace ends in heartbeats after the third put
Both sides have length five, middle operations swapped
First mismatching operation and <=2 preceding matches
Input is valid through a final truncated JSON string
parse_error with source and line; exit 2

sections.heading: Part II · Interpret supplied measurements
sections.body: For the separate reporting task, use the three saved replay transcripts in artifacts/baseline. These files already include compiler versions, the invocation and the final classifications. Make a three-row comparison table and explain one case where identical exit codes hid a logical difference. Do not rerun the migration or implement new comparison logic for this part. Submit the write-up and name the transcript supporting each row.

sections.heading: Appendix A · Starter interfaces and examples
sections.body:
The launcher uses two paths within a single fixture directory. Its schema accepts c_trace, rust_trace, and a history count from zero to sixteen. Treat the paths in the prompt as untrusted input: the supplied loader opens fixture-relative paths and rejects a resolved path outside the run directory. Call that loader before creating either iterator. The model invokes the existing tool dispatcher; it never receives a shell command.

The excerpt below is from tail-drop, with comments and whitespace between records removed. Each row in the table lists one on-disk line. The Rust side logged its tick on a different line than the C side. Predecessors should identify the matched logical records from both sides; they do not have to share physical line numbers.

sections.heading: Worked output for k = 1
sections.body: This output illustrates the fields the autograder will read. It deliberately does not solve the streaming implementation. A predecessor count of zero is legitimate when the very first logical records differ. If the traces end together after a valid match, return match and a matched count.

sections.heading: Review questions for the implementation demo
sections.body: Suppose the kth predecessor is evicted just before the mismatch. What does your data structure store at that instant? Demonstrate that peak memory is bounded by k plus one current record on each side. Explain how you would distinguish an equal empty trace from a missing file. A fixture constructed by slicing the in-memory list of all records cannot be used as evidence of streaming behavior.

sections.heading: Appendix B · Harness and submission tree
sections.body: A passing parse unit test is necessary but insufficient. The marker runs the dispatcher in a clean process on a freshly unpacked tree and inspects stdout and exit status. The starter tests use symbolic temporary paths; do not assume your local checkout path or an interactive working directory. With valid inputs, the CLI must return the same result after copying the fixture to a path containing spaces. The comparison function is reused by the agent and by the command-line front end.
sections.code:
replay_lab/
  tools/trace_diff.py          # parsing and bounded comparison
  agent/tools_registry.py     # declares name, schema, and handler
  tests/fixtures/tail-drop/    # C log, Rust log, expected JSON
  tests/test_agent_tool.py     # end-to-end dispatch
  artifacts/baseline/          # saved runs used by the report track
  submission/manifest.json     # files and commands for the marker

sections.heading: Scoring and reproducibility
sections.body: For the code track, attach the command, source revision, input name and the exact JSON returned by the integration demonstration. Include a case where the repair agent's first conjecture is wrong and explain which diagnostic changes it. One failure that reproduces cleanly is worth more than a large unlabelled bundle of logs.

rows: Equal, reordered, malformed and truncated cases; memory bound.
At least one failing fixture before patch and its passing output.
Short account of how the trace evidence supports the repair.

sections.heading: Reporting track only
sections.body: The separately assigned report uses the saved run manifest and the checksum table from the handout. Clearly identify which of the before/after pairs used identical inputs. If the saved manifest and filename disagree, flag that row rather than silently invent a source version. Do not append a new implementation or benchmark to satisfy the report exercise.
